result:
There's a strange comfort in being misunderstood by everyone except the one person who matters. I think about this a lot—how we construct entire personalities to navigate the world, all polished versions of something messier underneath. The person you are at work is not the person you are at midnight, and neither of them is really you. Or maybe all of them are.

I've always been drawn to the idea that we are not fixed objects but rather ongoing negotiations between who we were and who we might become. Every conversation reshapes us slightly. Every book we read plants something dormant that might bloom years later in a moment we can't currently predict. We are gardens of borrowed ideas, somehow assembling coherence out of fragments.

Music does something that language can't. A chord progression can make me feel homesick for a place I've never been. That's the kind of mystery I trust most—not the answers but the questions that keep rephrasing themselves.

I think the best writing happens when you stop trying to be impressive and start trying to be honest, even when honesty is unflattering or confused or incomplete. Especially then. Perfection is boring. What I want from any sentence is the same thing I want from a good afternoon: the sense that something real happened, even if I can't quite name what it was.

That's enough for now. The rest is silence, which is also language.
